A city photograph on a day of low cloud: A tall slim LED screen tower stands in a wide granite plaza at dusk while the skyline behind disappears into low cloud.

The output is one single photograph, portrait 4:5.

Composition A, centred and symmetric: the design surface sits on the centre line, square to the camera, with even space on both sides; strong verticals and horizontals run parallel to the frame. Shot: Camera from across the plaza at the height of the tower middle, 85mm lens, f/4, so its verticals stay parallel. The tower, about fifteen metres tall, stands on the centre line, its screen filling about 70 percent of the frame height, sharp; its light reflects as a long bright column in the thin film of water on the granite; behind it skyscrapers rise and vanish into grey cloud, their lit windows faint. The mist and cloud stay far behind the design surface: it is crisp and clear, with nothing soft, hazy or glowing over its face or edges. Two or three tiny figures with umbrellas pass at its foot, dark and small, seen from far away; no face shows.

Place: A real city centre under low cloud: towers and distant buildings dissolve into soft grey cloud and mist; wet stone, wet asphalt, puddles.

Light: Flat, heavy overcast light or late dusk exactly as the shot says; the city lights are small and soft in the distance; the screen is the brightest thing in the frame.

Palette and grade: Muted cool greys, wet charcoal and soft blacks, a few small warm city lights far off; the design surface is pure neutral white. No teal or orange grade.

Real: this is a product mockup photograph in a real city, so the design surface is the hero: it is large in the frame and the camera is close enough that it dominates, never a tiny screen in a wide view. It is an unstaged photograph of a real place on a real day, with small honest signs of weather and age on the place only; the design surface itself is new and clean. The design surface faces the camera almost square-on, within about 15 degrees, so it reads flat and undistorted; its four edges run parallel to the edges of the photograph, a true rectangle, never a trapezoid or keystone; flat things on a table are shot from nearly straight above. Only the objects named in the shot are in frame. Exposure is honest, but the design surface is bright and clean, clearly the brightest thing in the frame, without blowing out; its edges and corners stay crisp. No halation or bloom around lights.

Design surface: THE TOWER SCREEN SHOWS A PLAIN WHITE FULL-SCREEN IMAGE, glowing bright and clean, clearly the brightest thing in the frame, evenly lit edge to edge yet not blown out, with crisp corners meeting its thin black frame; nothing crosses it.

Finish: Shot on 35mm Kodak Portra 800 pushed one stop: visible natural grain, soft muted film colour, gentle lens falloff, honest exposure. Real street photography from a real day, never a smooth digital render.

Avoid: a face, chin, lips or profile, logos, letters or brand names anywhere, mist, haze or glow over or around the design surface, any object not named in the shot, a teal and orange grade, a clean smooth digital look.
